analysis: The reference image shows a wheeled trash bin whose expected articulated parts are a hinged lid (revolute) and two wheels (continuous). The generated model predicts exactly three joints with correct type labels — J1 is revolute and J2 / J3 are continuous, matching the expected revolute+continuous+continuous profile. However, the parent–child topology is entirely inverted: all three joints use the lid as the parent link, so J1 rotates the main bin body around the lid, and J2 / J3 rotate the wheels around the lid as well. This is physically unreasonable: the body should be the static base (with the lid rotating relative to it) and the wheels should spin about the body, not about the lid. The types themselves are right, so the model earns partial credit rather than the full deduction — score 2.
